spots.name: Mumbai Trans Harbour Link
spots.summary: The Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, officially named as Atal Bihari Vajpayee Sewri–Nhava Sheva Atal Setu and colloquially known as Atal Setu, is a 18.2 km (11.3 mi), 6-lane grade separated expressway bridge, which connects Mumbai with Navi Mumbai, its satellite city.

spots.name: Belapur Fort
spots.summary: Belapur Fort is a fort near the township of Belapur in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. The fort was built by the Siddhis of Janjira. It was later conquered by the Portuguese, and then Marathas. In the early 19th century, the fort was captured by the British.

spots.name: DY Patil Stadium
spots.summary: The DY Patil Stadium is a multi-purpose sports arena in Navi Mumbai, Maharashtra, India. Owned by Dnyandeo Yashwantrao Patil, it is based in the DY Patil Sports Academy in Nerul. It is primarily a cricket stadium, though it is sometimes used for football, music concerts and other events.

spots.name: Utsav Chowk
spots.summary: One of the most famous landmarks in the area and it stands out for its eye catching architecture which is a humble reflection of the Roman and Greek architecture.

spots.name: Central Park
spots.summary: The project of Central Park is to make a public park with Navi Mumbai's ethos reflected into the future. It is under construction but is open to public. The large amphitheatre has hosted many public shows. An ISKCON temple is attached to this park. To the west of this park is Pandav Kada waterfall and CIDCO developed golf course.
